verdict.rationale: DeepSeek's own docs describe a Context Caching on Disk feature that is on by default and needs no code changes, so the core caching capability is first-party and documented. The pack contains no cache-hit pricing and no evidence of the actual cost or latency savings, which are half of the story. Missing for 10: documented cache-hit vs cache-miss pricing, evidence of latency reduction, details on cache matching (prefix rules/TTL), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ml-engineer, I can cut cost and latency on repeated context with documented prompt/prefix caching and its pricing

citations.quote: The DeepSeek API Context Caching on Disk Technology is enabled by default for all users, allowing them to benefit without needing to modify their code.
